name: Dorm Room Fund (student-run pre-seed fund)
what_you_get: Pre-seed equity checks decided by student investment teams. Recent reporting says student teams write $40,000 checks; other third-party profiles cite larger ranges ($90K-$500K) after the new fund, which DRF's own site does not confirm. In late Sept 2026 DRF closed a new $50M fund (about 4x the prior fund) for student and alumni founders. Around 60 student investors a year across about 30 campuses, with professional oversight on terms and diligence.
eligibility: At least one founder must be a current student or recent graduate (per University Business reporting).
timing: New $50M fund announced late Sept 2026. Founder application window not shown in snippets. 2026 student Investment Partner recruitment closed 9/17 (Philly & Southeast, NY & Midwest, Boston & Northeast) and 10/1 (SF & West Coast).
fit_why: SimReal clearly meets the student-founder test through Amaris (Duke), and a freshly raised $50M fund means capital is available now. Duke falls in DRF's Philly & Southeast region.

contacts.name: Christina Liang
contacts.role: Student Investment Partner, Dorm Room Fund Philly & Southeast team; described as a Duke senior (Statistics and French). The interview is undated, so she may have graduated.

contacts.name: Madison Jacox
contacts.role: Named as part of DRF's professional oversight on terms and diligence (title not verified)

name: Rough Draft Ventures
what_you_get: Student-run pre-seed fund backed by General Catalyst. A third-party profile says student scouts write $25,000 checks. Portfolio companies also get coaching from General Catalyst partners and RDV alumni. The fund has backed more than 150 startups.
eligibility: Student founders across North American universities (the network spans NA campuses). Whether Duke is a covered campus was not confirmed.
timing: Founder pitches are not tied to a published cycle. Student investor recruiting opens each March, with decisions in late April.
how_to_apply: https://roughdraft.vc (pitch through a campus student investor)
fit_why: General Catalyst offers a student-founder on-ramp, but the checks are small and RDV historically centers on Boston and Northeast campuses.

name: Contrary (Venture Partner program / Contrary Capital)
what_you_get: Contrary recruits a selective class of student Venture Partners at US and Canadian universities each year to source and back founders. The firm itself invests seed to Series A; a third-party profile cites $100K-$2M checks with a $500K-$1M sweet spot.
eligibility: No published student-only rule. Student founders are typically sourced through campus Venture Partners. Class of 2026 VPs were announced.
timing: Rolling investment. Venture Partner applications for 2026 were posted on Contrary's blog.
how_to_apply: https://contrary.com (reach the firm directly or through a Duke Venture Partner if one is listed in the Class of 2026 post)
fit_why: Talent-driven seed firm that writes seed-sized checks and fits a technical AI team. Its student VP network is a warm route in.

name: Z Fellows
what_you_get: A one-week program of 10 builders with mentors from top tech companies. Fellows can take an optional $10,000 investment at a $1B valuation cap that converts at the next priced round. Mostly virtual, with a last day in person in SF or NYC.
eligibility: No age restriction. Apply solo or with co-founders. Aimed at technical builders.
timing: Rolling, with no deadline and multiple cohorts a year.
fit_why: Fast, cheap and nearly non-dilutive given the $1B cap, with strong SF network value. The money itself is small.

name: Neo Scholars
what_you_get: 2026 terms: a $40,000 equity-free grant to college students, a 3-month SF summer residency, mentorship, recruiting fast-track, and meetups in NY, SF and Boston. Scholars who start a company get guaranteed admission to the Neo Residency.
eligibility: Current college students who excel at computer science. North America only.
timing: The 2026 cycle opened in May 2026 and closed June 14, 2026. The 2027 cycle is expected in spring 2027 but is not confirmed.
fit_why: It's non-dilutive money for an individual student and a route into the Neo Residency. It only fits if Amaris has a strong CS profile.

name: Neo Residency (startup track)
what_you_get: A third-party guide reports a $750,000 uncapped SAFE plus participation rights up to 5% ownership.
eligibility: Startup teams. North America only, per the same guide.
timing: 2026-27 cycle dates were not found.
fit_why: Large uncapped check from a selective, technical-founder network. It's unclear whether a US/UK team counts as 'North America'.

name: Pareto Fellowship / Pareto20
what_you_get: Pareto Holdings (Jon Oringer, Ed Lando) runs a fellowship offering funding, operational support and mentorship. Its inaugural cohort was a five-day virtual program for 17 young innovators. Pareto Holdings is an active seed investor (57-58 investments as of mid-2026).
eligibility: Aimed at the next generation of young tech entrepreneurs. Current age and student criteria were not found. Pareto20 terms were not found.
timing: No 2026-27 cycle found.
how_to_apply: Pareto Holdings website (application URL not found)
fit_why: The young-founder focus fits, but there is no current cycle or published terms.

name: Soma Capital Fellowship
what_you_get: $100,000 on an uncapped SAFE, with access to up to $2M in follow-on funding, concierge support, office space and customer intros. Fully remote, with optional in-person events.
eligibility: Originally for student founders and now open to anyone building an early-stage company; skews to founders in their early to mid 20s. Global, with no relocation.
timing: The 2026 application deadline was April 1, 2026. The next cycle date was not found.
how_to_apply: https://superscout.co/program/soma-capital-fellowship (official Soma Capital fellowship page; URL not confirmed)
fit_why: An uncapped $100K with no relocation suits a distributed US/UK team of ~21-year-olds. Watch for the 2027 window.

name: a16z speedrun (SR008)
what_you_get: $500K for 10% on a SAFE upfront, plus $500K in the next round within 18 months (up to $1M), and $5M+ in partner credits.
eligibility: Early-stage founders. Not student-specific. In person in SF for the cohort.
timing: SR007 ran July 27-Oct 11, 2026. SR008 runs late January-April 2027 in SF. Applications are rolling, reviewed in about 4-6 weeks. A third-party guide reports a priority window of Oct 12-Nov 1; the year is unconfirmed.
fit_why: AI-friendly and a16z-branded, which helps a seed raise. However, 10% for $500K is expensive and the cohort requires SF relocation.

contacts.name: Kenan Saleh
contacts.role: Posted the a16z speedrun application announcement on X (title not verified)

name: Afore Capital - Founders-in-Residence (incl. FIR University)
what_you_get: Afore runs an 8-week Founders-in-Residence program (cohorts of 5-8; e.g. $50K and a desk) and a university track, 'FIR University', reported to provide $20K-$100K. Fund IV ($185M, 'Pre-Seed 2.0') writes flexible $50K-$2M pre-seed checks.
eligibility: The university track is for founders still in college. Pre-seed generally.
timing: 2026-27 cohort dates were not found.
how_to_apply: Afore Capital website (FIR application URL not found)
fit_why: A dedicated pre-seed firm with a college-founder track. It may suit SimReal's pre-seed/seed raise better than its residency.

name: KP Fellows (2027)
what_you_get: A paid summer fellowship working inside a Kleiner Perkins portfolio company in the Bay Area, with a founder speaker series and workshops. Alumni join a 1,000+ community and get continuing KP support for entrepreneurial work.
eligibility: Individual students with CS, engineering, math, physics or related degrees (Engineering track). There is also a Design track. Must be in the SF Bay Area for the summer.
timing: Applications are open until Jan 31, 2027 (11:59pm PST), reviewed on a rolling basis.
fit_why: It's an internship for an individual, not company funding, and would pull Amaris away from SimReal for the summer. The value is the KP network only.

name: PearX (W27)
what_you_get: A 12-week accelerator in SF with $250K-$2M investment (terms negotiated by stage). Includes mentorship, hiring support, customer intros and cloud credits. About 20 teams per cohort.
eligibility: Pre-seed/seed founders. Teams must relocate to the SF Bay Area.
timing: W27 regular deadline: Oct 4 (11:59pm PST), i.e. today, per a third-party listing. S26 ran Feb 10-Apr 12, 2026.
fit_why: Strong seed-stage partner with flexible check sizes. The deadline is today and the program needs SF relocation. The Pear Competition (below) is the student route.

name: Pear Competition (Pear Dorm)
what_you_get: Winners get a $100K uncapped SAFE (no discount), up to $350K in cloud credits and tech benefits, and a fast-track PearX partner meeting. Runners-up may receive $25K or $50K investments. Pear Dorm programs (Competition, Garage) give student cohorts $10K-$100K each.
eligibility: At least one team member must be a current student at a US or Canadian university. Incorporation not required.
timing: The 2026-27 competition schedule was not found. Teams can apply to the Competition and PearX at the same time.
fit_why: Amaris's Duke enrollment alone satisfies the rule. The prize is a meaningful uncapped check plus a fast path into PearX.

name: 1517 Fund (Medici Grants and student/dropout pre-seed)
what_you_get: Medici Project grants give a minimum $1K stipend with zero equity, zero IP and no future claim. Separately, 1517 Fund (run by the people who ran the Thiel Fellowship) is reported to run a $175M fund for dropouts and students.
eligibility: Medici: high school students, college students or dropouts working on passion projects not for school credit.
timing: Medici grants are rolling. No specific 2026-27 deadline found.
fit_why: The grant is tiny. The 1517 fund itself is the more relevant contact for SimReal's raise.

name: Thiel Fellowship
what_you_get: $250,000 over two years (doubled from $100K in 2024). 12 fellows selected in 2026.
eligibility: Age 22 or younger, no university degree, and must drop out or stop out of school to accept.
timing: A third-party listing shows a Dec 31, 2026 date (unconfirmed). Historically rolling.
how_to_apply: Thiel Fellowship website (thielfellowship.org; URL from listings, not read)
fit_why: Amaris would have to leave Duke, and the Cambridge/LSE graduates already hold degrees, so the team as constituted does not qualify.

name: Emergent Ventures (incl. EV AI)
what_you_get: Grants and fellowships led by Tyler Cowen, reported as typically $10K-$100K (most around $50K), plus travel and project grants. EV AI is a dedicated vertical for AI researchers and entrepreneurs.
eligibility: Open worldwide, age 13+, with no institutional affiliation required. Covers entrepreneurs, researchers and students.
timing: Rolling. The application takes about 30 minutes and decisions can come within days.
fit_why: Fast, non-dilutive and AI-focused. EV favors individuals with bold ideas, so pitch the founders, e.g. on open RL-environment research.

name: AI Grant
what_you_get: Last published terms: $250K uncapped SAFE, $350K in Azure credits and about $250K in partner credits (Anthropic, OpenAI, Modal and others), about $850K in total value.
eligibility: Seed-stage AI startups. Not student-specific.
timing: Batch 4 is listed as closed. No 2026-27 batch found.
fit_why: Ideal AI-native terms if a new batch opens. Its continuation is uncertain.

name: HF0 Residency
what_you_get: A 12-week in-person SF residency with housing and meals, and up to $1M on an uncapped SAFE for 5%. About 10 teams per cohort.
eligibility: Aimed at repeat and high-performing technical founders. AI and deep tech focus. Requires full-time SF residency.
timing: Fall 2026 cohort. A third-party listing says rolling applications are accepted until late 2026.
how_to_apply: HF0 website (hf0.com; application URL not confirmed)
fit_why: Large, founder-friendly terms for AI teams. Very selective, biased to repeat founders, and needs full SF relocation.

name: SPC Founder Fellowship
what_you_get: $400K upfront for 7% on a standard SAFE, plus $600K guaranteed in the next external round ($1M total). Includes SPC membership, partner working sessions and $900K+ in credits (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, GCP, AWS and others).
eligibility: Pre-idea to early founders. No traction required. Not student-specific.
timing: Fall 2026 applications closed Aug 2, 2026. The Spring 2027 cycle has not been announced in the results found.
fit_why: Strong seed-equivalent terms and credits. Watch for the next cycle.

name: Entrepreneur First
what_you_get: A £6,000 talent investment on signing. The US pathway invests up to $250K ($125K post-money SAFE for 8% plus a $125K uncapped MFN SAFE) after forming a Delaware C-corp. London and Bangalore cohorts spend 12 weeks at home, then 12 weeks in SF.
eligibility: Individuals before they have a co-founder or idea. The 2026 application is solo.
timing: London Fall 2026 started in September 2026. SF runs continuously.
fit_why: EF builds teams from individuals, and SimReal already has a team and product.

name: Y Combinator (W27, incl. Early Decision for students)
what_you_get: $500K: $125K for 7% plus $375K on a SAFE. Includes a dedicated GP, the alumni network and $12M+ in partner credits. Early Decision lets students apply while in school, get accepted and funded, and defer the batch until after graduation.
eligibility: Open to founders including students. In person in SF for the batch.
timing: W27 (Jan-Mar 2027, SF) on-time deadline is Nov 2, 2026 at 8pm PT, with decisions by Dec 11. Late applications are considered without a promised timeline.
fit_why: The most valuable seed signal available. Early Decision means Amaris can stay at Duke and the team can still lock in YC.

name: Interact Fellowship
what_you_get: A two-year fellowship with fully sponsored retreats twice a year in a global community of young technologists. 50 new fellows a year. No startup funding.
eligibility: Individuals aged 18-23 with an interest in technology broadly understood.
timing: The 2026 class deadline was Feb 9, 2026. The 2027 cycle is expected in early 2027 but not confirmed.
fit_why: Founders are the right age, but it's network-only with a social-impact tilt and no capital.

name: Prelude / 'Leadership grants' (requested; not identified)
what_you_get: No program matching 'Prelude' or 'Leadership grants' for student founders was found in searches.
eligibility: not found
timing: not found
fit_why: The founders should confirm which program was meant.

name: America's Startup national competition (America250)
what_you_get: A $1M total non-dilutive prize pool. 10 finalist teams get $25,000 each, and 3 overall winners get another $25,000 ($50K total). Includes national mentorship and a live pitch finale. The top 100 entries go to an Investors Council for optional equity investment, and entrants get an NVIDIA Inception invitation.
eligibility: US legal residents 13+ who are current undergraduates at an accredited US university, college or trade school. Individuals or teams of up to 5.
timing: Opened Aug 17, 2026. Closes Oct 8, 2026 at 7:59pm EDT (4 days away). Requires a written proposal and a short pitch video.
fit_why: Non-dilutive money that closes this week. It hinges on Amaris being a US legal resident and on whether non-student co-founders can be on the team; if not, Amaris could enter alone.

name: Rice Business Plan Competition 2027
what_you_get: More than $1M in investment and cash prizes expected for 2027. Every startup gets a minimum prize for its placement: no-equity cash, investor prizes, accelerator invitations and in-kind prizes.
eligibility: Teams need at least two current students, at least one of them a graduate student. Startups must be student-driven, student-created or student-managed. Must be fundraising within 12 months. Digital enterprise is an eligible sector.
timing: Competition Apr 8-10, 2027 in Houston. The 2027 application deadline was not found; the 2026 deadline was Jan 31, 2026.
fit_why: The richest student competition, but SimReal needs a current graduate student on the team to qualify.

name: ACC InVenture Prize 2027
what_you_get: $30,000 in cash: $15K for 1st, $10K for 2nd and $5K for People's Choice. Televised finals.
eligibility: Teams of full-time, degree-seeking undergraduates or recent graduates within one year of their undergraduate degree, representing an ACC school (Duke qualifies). Revenue or capital raised must not exceed $100K. Each school nominates its team.
timing: Faculty rep application due Jan 23, 2027; student team rep application due Jan 30, 2027; pitch video due Feb 17, 2027; finals Mar 16-17, 2027.
fit_why: Duke is an ACC school. SimReal fails the cap if it has raised over $100K, and team rules may exclude the non-Duke founders.

name: Hult Prize 2027
what_you_get: $1M seed funding to the winning team.
eligibility: All 2-4 team members must be enrolled in a degree program and be 18+ by Feb 28, 2027. The for-profit venture must directly support at least one UN SDG.
timing: The competition started Sept 1, 2026. Deadlines vary by route and phase.
fit_why: The recent-graduate founders are not enrolled, and an RL-environments business is a weak fit for the SDG requirement.

name: New Venture Championship
what_you_get: Discontinued: the University of Oregon replaced the NVC with the Oregon Innovation Challenge in 2023.
eligibility: n/a
timing: No 2026-27 edition.
fit_why: The competition no longer runs.

name: Wake Forest Elevator Competition
org: Wake Forest University School of Business
what_you_get: Historically $10,000 cash for the first-place Traditional Business winner and $5,000 for the top Social Entrepreneurship team.
eligibility: Historically teams of up to 4 with at least one currently enrolled degree-seeking student (graduate or undergraduate).
timing: No 2026-27 edition or deadline found. Latest news found covers editions from about a decade ago.
fit_why: Small prize, and it's unclear whether the competition still runs.

name: Venture Capital Investment Competition (VCIC) - startup pitch slot
what_you_get: Real startups pitch to student 'VC firm' teams and VC judges, go through six due-diligence sessions and negotiate term sheets. More than 25% of participating startups later raise VC. No cash prize for startups was found.
eligibility: Startups apply to be pitch companies (3 per regional). Students act as the VCs, so this is not a founder competition.
timing: External Regional on Feb 2, 2027 at Fordham Gabelli (NYC). Global Finals Apr 16-17, 2027 at UNC Kenan-Flagler (Chapel Hill, near Duke).
fit_why: Gives VC-judge exposure and pitch practice near Duke, but no capital.

name: Collegiate Inventors Competition 2027
what_you_get: Cash prizes up to $10,000, an all-expenses-paid finalist trip to Washington, D.C., and a patent acceleration certificate.
eligibility: Full- or part-time students at US colleges, any nationality, undergraduate or graduate. Requires an original invention, an essay and a faculty or professional reference.
timing: Expected to open April 2027. Deadline June 1, 2027.
fit_why: Invention- and patent-oriented. An RL environment or verifier would be a stretch, though a novel verifier method could be entered.

name: Big Ideas
what_you_get: Not verified: the search budget ran out before this was checked.
eligibility: not verified
timing: not verified
fit_why: Not verified; may be restricted to UC students.

name: Microsoft Imagine Cup 2027
what_you_get: Global student-startup competition on Microsoft cloud and AI. The 2026 winner received $150,000 and a mentorship session with Satya Nadella; 2027 prize amounts were not confirmed.
eligibility: Teams of up to 4. All members must be enrolled students aged 18+. Launch track: no dilutive funding and at most $100K non-dilutive. Scale track: at most $5M combined funding. (Snippet eligibility dates referenced the 2025-26 cycle.)
timing: Registration and submission deadline Jan 8, 2027. Regional semifinals in spring 2027 and the world championship in May 2027.
fit_why: AI-focused and global. The rule that all members be students excludes graduated co-founders unless only current students enter.

name: Red Bull Basement
what_you_get: 2026: the World Final winner received $100,000, $25,000 in Microsoft Azure credits and mentorship from Red Bull Ventures. The top 65 US ideas submit videos, 15 finalists pitch at the US National Final, and 3 US teams go to the World Final in SF.
eligibility: 2026 US rules: legal US residents 18+, individually or in teams of up to 2. One-page AI-assisted business proposal.
timing: The 2026 cycle closed Mar 29, 2026. A 2027 cycle was not found.
fit_why: Teams are capped at 2 and US residency is required. The 2027 cycle is unconfirmed.

name: Columbia AI Startup Challenge
what_you_get: $40K+ in total prizes for AI-driven startup ideas.
eligibility: Graduate students at Columbia, Cornell Tech, NYU or Yale only.
timing: 2026 edition held. No 2027 dates found.
fit_why: SimReal has no eligible graduate student at these schools; listed only to show it was checked.

name: GitHub Student Developer Pack
what_you_get: A bundle of free student offers. Examples: Azure $100/yr, MongoDB Atlas $50 plus certifications, Heroku $13/month for 24 months, DigitalOcean credit.
eligibility: Verified students. Amaris qualifies individually.
timing: Ongoing.
fit_why: Easy to claim through Amaris, but the amounts are tiny next to startup programs.

name: AWS Activate
what_you_get: Up to $200,000 in credits for eligible startups. The Founders package gives $1,000 to self-funded startups. No separate student or university path was confirmed in searches.
eligibility: Startups. Higher tiers come via provider or accelerator referral.
timing: Ongoing.
fit_why: Useful compute for RL environments. The student angle is weak; the bigger tiers come through accelerator partners such as Pear, SPC and speedrun.

name: Google for Startups Cloud Program
what_you_get: $2,000 for pre-funded startups, up to $200,000 for seed to Series A, and up to $350,000 reported for AI-first startups.
eligibility: Startups. No student-specific track was confirmed.
timing: Ongoing.
how_to_apply: Google for Startups Cloud Program site (URL not read)
fit_why: Largest AI-first credit tier, useful for model and environment compute. Not student-specific.

name: Microsoft for Startups (Founders Hub) / Azure for Students
what_you_get: Microsoft for Startups: $5,000 in Azure credits plus Microsoft 365 and GitHub access (third-party figure). Azure for Students: $100 credit for 12 months, renewable, for full-time students.
eligibility: Startups. Azure for Students needs an enrolled student (Amaris).
timing: Ongoing.
how_to_apply: Microsoft for Startups site (URL not read)
fit_why: Modest credits. The Imagine Cup and AI Grant historically carry larger Azure grants.

name: Anthropic - Claude for Startups / Claude Campus
what_you_get: Claude for Startups credit tiers: $5K by direct application, $25K with a VC or accelerator partner referral, and up to $100K for startups backed by top-tier VCs. Also priority rate limits. Student angle: Claude Campus ambassadors get a $3,600 cash stipend, and Builder Clubs share resources such as API credits.
eligibility: Credits need institutional equity funding, a company under 4 years old, and no prior Anthropic credits. Any early-stage founder can apply to the broader program.
timing: Direct applications open since late May 2026.
fit_why: Directly relevant to an LLM post-training company. Ask the lead seed investor for a partner referral code to reach the $25K-$100K tiers.

name: OpenAI startup credits
what_you_get: Not verified (search budget). OpenAI credits do appear as perks inside SPC Founder Fellowship and AI Grant packages.
eligibility: not verified
timing: not verified
fit_why: Most accessible through accelerator packages rather than a student path.

name: NVIDIA Inception
what_you_get: Free, with no equity or fees. Includes SDKs, Deep Learning Institute credits, hardware and software pricing, and investor and go-to-market support. Third-party sources report up to $100K in DGX Cloud credits at entry tier and 30% off DGX Cloud. Entrants to America's Startup get an Inception invitation.
eligibility: AI startups globally. Not student-specific.
timing: Rolling.
fit_why: Free and relevant for GPU-heavy RL work. Join now.

name: Modal / Lambda compute credits
what_you_get: Modal: startup program up to $50K in credits. The academics program (up to $25K) is for faculty, postdocs and PhD students, not undergraduates, and the $10K academic grant was reported paused. A third-party site cites $30/month free compute for students. Lambda: Research Grant up to $5K in GPU credits for researchers.
eligibility: Modal startup program: startups. Modal academics and Lambda grants: researchers, so an undergraduate founder is unlikely to qualify.
timing: Rolling.
fit_why: Modal's startup tier is useful for running environments. The student and academic paths largely don't fit undergraduate founders.
